tagline.text: A quiet island beside a strait where manta rays gather

budget.label: Budget

children.text: An island of Masbate province across the Ticao Pass from the waters off Sorsogon, a hidden gem for divers thanks to the "Manta Bowl," an undersea seamount where reef manta rays gather year-round. From Catandayagan Falls, which drops straight into the sea, to island hopping among white sand bars, it's a chance to enjoy island life untouched by mass tourism.

Ticao is a long, narrow island lying between Sorsogon, at the southern tip of the Bicol Peninsula, and the main island of Masbate. Administratively part of Masbate province, it's divided among four towns: San Jacinto, San Fernando, Batuan, and Monreal. To its west, the Ticao Pass runs between the island and the Bicol mainland; strong currents through this channel, which links the Pacific to the Sibuyan Sea, carry plankton that draw large marine life to these waters.

The star of this sea is the manta ray. About 7km off the island's west coast, a small seamount rises from a seafloor 200m deep, and its summit, at roughly 14–25m depth, serves as a "cleaning station" where mantas come to have parasites removed. Divers call this spot the "Manta Bowl," and research groups have individually cataloged hundreds of reef mantas here, making it one of the Philippines' largest reef manta habitats. With luck, you might also encounter whale sharks and thresher sharks. The strait is designated as part of the Ticao-Burias Pass Protected Seascape.

The scenery above water is just as good. Catandayagan Falls, dropping straight from a cliff on the island's west side into the sea, is a rare "waterfall into the ocean" in the Philippines, and off Monreal, hopping points like the white sand islet of Halea and the rock formation Borobangkaso are scattered about. Inland, the island is classic Masbate countryside — cattle-grazing pastures and coconut groves.

With few amenities and multiple transport transfers required, this isn't a mainstream destination. That means fewer crowds and cheaper prices, making it worth recommending to divers with drift-diving experience, travelers who want to see Bicol's waters in depth by combining this with the Donsol whale shark tour, and anyone willing to accept some inconvenience in exchange for a quiet island.
From a dive center on the island's west side, head out by boat for about
15–30 minutes
and ride the current to the manta cleaning station atop the seamount. Strong currents mean a reef hook is used, making this an intermediate-or-above dive.
A waterfall dropping straight into the sea from a cliff about
high. Approach by boat from the water and you can swim right beneath the falls.
A small island off Monreal with fine white sand and clear water, used as the lunch and swimming stop on hopping tours. The shallow coral area is good for snorkeling.
A rocky islet carved by the waves; climb the stairs to the top of the rock for a sweeping view of the surrounding sea and islands. A popular photo spot.
On the island's west side, vertical wall dive sites descend past soft coral and sea whips, while shallow coral gardens are good for spotting small critters like frogfish and nudibranchs.

Rent an outrigger boat from Monreal port to tour Halea Island, Borobangkaso, and the Ginlatayan rock formation in a single day. Boats can be split among up to 5 people, making it economical for a group.

March–June

, when the sea is calmest, is the best time. Visibility improves during this period, and whale sharks often appear in the Ticao Pass and off Donsol too, making it easy to combine both. Midday temperatures run around
July–October

is the rainy and typhoon season, and when a typhoon crosses the Bicol region, boats can stop running for days at a time. On the other hand, divers have reported better chances of encountering thresher sharks during this period.
November–February
brings the northeast monsoon Amihan, which roughens the strait and brings frequent rain, so if diving is your goal, it's wise to build in two or more weather buffer days.

Accommodation options are limited. If diving is your goal, staying at a resort that also runs a dive center, such as Ticao Island Resort on the island's west coast, is essentially your only option, at about

a night with meals included. Diving is mostly run for guests, and walk-in day divers often aren't accepted, so booking ahead is essential. In Monreal and San Jacinto towns, fan-room homestays and small beach resorts are available at about
a night.
The food here is simple. At a town karinderia (eatery with pre-cooked dishes), rice plus a choice of two dishes runs about

a meal, and on island-hopping trips, the boatman often grills fish, squid, and crab for lunch. Masbate is one of the Philippines' leading cattle-raising areas, so bulalo (beef bone marrow soup) and other beef dishes are common and good. Bicolano dishes simmered in coconut milk, and kinilaw (fish cured in vinegar), are also popular. Outside the resorts, cafés and Western-style restaurants are scarce, so it's worth bringing your own snacks and coffee.
The island has almost no ATMs, and the few there often malfunction. Withdraw plenty of small-denomination cash in Pilar or Sorsogon City for your whole stay.

The Manta Bowl is a drift dive with currents reaching 2–3 knots, so Advanced Open Water certification or above and drift-diving experience are recommended. Be sure to bring your logbook and certification card.
A reef hook and an SMB (surface marker buoy) are essential gear. Check in advance whether the dive center rents them out.
Catandayagan Falls looks best viewed from the sea, and flows fullest for a few days after rain. Toward the end of the dry season, the flow can thin out.
Boats from Pilar to Monreal cluster in the morning, with few or none in the afternoon on many days, so it's best to arrive at Bicol International Airport on a morning flight.
If you're combining this with the Donsol whale shark tour, Donsol and Pilar are about 40 minutes apart by car, so you can continue on the same day.
Power sometimes cuts out in the evening, so a power bank and flashlight come in handy. Phone signal is stable only near town centers.

The Manta Bowl can be dangerous for beginners due to strong currents and depth. Only dive sites that match your certification level, and follow the rule of staying on the bottom in front of the cleaning station to observe, without touching or chasing the mantas.
Small outrigger boats rock heavily in high waves and sailings are often canceled. Wear a life vest, and don't push ahead on days the coast guard has halted departures.
Masbate province has had reports of security incidents around election periods, so check local news and travel advisories before you go, and avoid traveling late at night.
The island has no major hospital or decompression chamber. Get dive insurance and avoid pushing through too many consecutive dives.
Collecting coral or shells and touching marine life are prohibited in the protected seascape, and environmental fee and admission rules can change, so check the on-site notice.
Wet rocks at the falls and rock islets are very slippery. Wear aqua shoes, and don't jump from height as if diving.
